Inflation Vigilante

Colin Suvak, CFA, Vice President, Research

Here, something stands out: the correlation between the two series is 65%, which places it in the 97th percentile historically. That is the highest level since the initial inflationary surge peaked in 2022. Exhibit 2 shows the trajectory of this series from late 2021, when global inflation first started to rise amid the COVID-19 pandemic.

Across countries, the relationship is clear: the higher the inflation rate, the steeper the yield curve tends to be. Since 1970, this series of correlations has averaged -21%; Exhibit 3 shows the recent stretch is quite abnormal.

Using AAI, we also examine other possible explanations for the higher slope, such as robust GDP growth. The connection is negligible, which indicates that inflation, rather than current or expected growth, is more closely associated with the unusually steep yield curves we see throughout the world today. So, while the bond vigilantes may indeed be trying to impose fiscal discipline, inflation seems to be what’s really shaping yield curves.

Categorizing the 21 countries into DMs and EMs presents another interesting takeaway: rising DM inflation is a relatively recent phenomenon. The average DM inflation rate is only about two percentage points lower than its average EM counterpart, which places it in the 17th percentile historically. In 2022, however, average EM inflation was five to six percentage points higher than average DM inflation. Since 2022, evidently, DM inflation has been comparatively stickier.

Higher inflation has more recently led to higher 10Y–3M slopes, as Exhibit 2 shows. Indeed, the average DM yield curve has steepened by 2.2 percentage points in the last couple years, compared to only 1.6 percentage points for its average EM peer. Japan provides perhaps the most salient example: Since December 2021, its yield curve slope has increased more than that of any country in the sample except Malaysia. At the same time, only Turkey, Indonesia, and Australia have eclipsed Japan in its annual inflation rate change. Exhibit 4, which shows Japan’s yield curve slope and inflation next to those of the United States, reveals the inflation vigilante at work.

Rising sovereign bond yields have important implications for expected returns across many asset classes. We encourage readers to explore AAI to see how the changing rate environment is influencing our current forecasts. Our analysis shows that resurgent inflation is driving these higher yield curves across the globe, but especially in developed markets.

While the bond vigilantes may be getting the headlines, the inflation vigilante is what we see in the data.

text:
New Slack app, smarter ZIP-code search, and a compliance update you need to know.

Apollo ( https://app.apollo.io/?utm_campaign=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree&utm_content=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree_EML_FREE_ProductNewsletter_F2P_EN&utm_medium=email&utm_source=cio )

*************************
Apollo now lives in Slack
*************************

Apollo and Slack logos on a colorful gradient background ( https://app.apollo.io/?utm_campaign=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree&utm_content=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree_EML_FREE_ProductNewsletter_F2P_EN&utm_medium=email&utm_source=cio#/assistant/channels )

Connect the new Apollo app to find leads that match your target audience, create sequences, check how they’re doing, and get workflow notifications without leaving Slack. Already have Apollo in Slack? Reconnect once to get the new updated version.

Connect Apollo to Slack ( https://app.apollo.io/?utm_campaign=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree&utm_content=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree_EML_FREE_ProductNewsletter_F2P_EN&utm_medium=email&utm_source=cio#/assistant/channels )
Learn more ( https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/22464817775117-Integrate-Slack-with-Apollo?utm_campaign=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree&utm_content=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree_EML_FREE_ProductNewsletter_F2P_EN&utm_medium=email&utm_source=cio )

 

Apollo search bar reading Find leading professionals, beside yellow map pins ( https://app.apollo.io/?utm_campaign=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree&utm_content=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree_EML_FREE_ProductNewsletter_F2P_EN&utm_medium=email&utm_source=cio#/people )

-------------------------------------
Get better search results by ZIP code
-------------------------------------

Get more complete search results, even when the postal-code field is blank. Apollo now recovers a ZIP code straight from the address whenever the city matches our records.

Try it now ( https://app.apollo.io/?utm_campaign=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree&utm_content=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree_EML_FREE_ProductNewsletter_F2P_EN&utm_medium=email&utm_source=cio#/people )

 

--------------------------------------
No more DNC labels for French contacts
--------------------------------------

France changed its telemarketing law ( https://www.economie.gouv.fr/dgccrf/actualites-dgccrf/le-demarchage-telephonique-desormais-interdit-si-vous-ny-avez-pas-consenti?utm_campaign=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree&utm_content=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree_EML_FREE_ProductNewsletter_F2P_EN&utm_medium=email&utm_source=cio ), and Bloctel, the Do-Not-Call (DNC) registry Apollo checked French numbers against, has shut down. If you have DNC enabled, Apollo is removing DNC tags from French numbers and will no longer check new French numbers for DNC. Visit our knowledge base ( https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/45502145803149-Protect-Your-Caller-Reputation-and-Stay-Compliant?utm_campaign=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree&utm_content=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree_EML_FREE_ProductNewsletter_F2P_EN&utm_medium=email&utm_source=cio ) to learn how to protect your caller reputation and stay compliant.

Learn more ( https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/45502145803149-Protect-Your-Caller-Reputation-and-Stay-Compliant?utm_campaign=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree&utm_content=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree_EML_FREE_ProductNewsletter_F2P_EN&utm_medium=email&utm_source=cio )

Illustration of a telephone with a red Do Not Call tag ( https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/45502145803149-Protect-Your-Caller-Reputation-and-Stay-Compliant?utm_campaign=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree&utm_content=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree_EML_FREE_ProductNewsletter_F2P_EN&utm_medium=email&utm_source=cio )

 

Keep up with everything we’re building

Bookmark our Release Notes to stay up to date on the latest Apollo product news and improvements.

View release notes ( https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/43226752968077-Release-Notes-2026?utm_campaign=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree&utm_content=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree_EML_FREE_ProductNewsletter_F2P_EN&utm_medium=email&utm_source=cio )

---------------------------------------
Save $120 or more on a paid Apollo plan
---------------------------------------

Save $120 or more on a paid plan with annual billing.* You’ll unlock more credits (starting at 30,000 credits per year or 2,500 per month) to find leads and engage prospects. Plus, you’ll get access to advanced search filters, Waterfall Enrichment for the highest-quality data, and more.

View plans ( https://app.apollo.io/?utm_campaign=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree&utm_content=20261008_NEWS_GLBL_OctoberProductNewsletterFree_EML_FREE_ProductNewsletter_F2P_EN&utm_medium=email&utm_source=cio#/settings/plans/upgrade?interval=yearly )

subj: Protect Your Account This Cybersecurity Awareness Month
text:
Six ways to help protect your account from scams.  Firstrade
Securities Inc. ( https://clicks.firstrade.com/f/a/awZiOVXHfpLfkfsNz4uFlg~~/AAQRxRA~/Rl9IwdaIiutLkqGUVHzy0TX2WuinS4BJAHdJk_xvyrkx5P9iFCcZu4_SLITPvITIytWHQwSpfUYP4aYLpeuLXpFvIH8M5am3r5nBIXd4WrirtGg1iMYjxiyxGtTdB6AX )   Dear
Tianlong,

October is Cybersecurity Awareness Month. With scam activity on
the rise across the industry, we'd like to share six simple steps
to help keep your account safe.

Check before you click.
-----------------------

Scammers send fake emails that look like they come from a
brokerage, often asking you to "update your tax information" or
"verify your account" through a button or link. Never click links
or buttons in suspicious emails.

Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA).
----------------------------------------

Multi-factor authentication is widely regarded as one of the
most effective ways to protect an account from unauthorized
access, and 2FA is how you can turn it on for your Firstrade
account. Each time you sign in, you'll enter a code from an
authentication app, so even if your password is stolen or
phished, it isn't enough to get into your account. We strongly
recommend every client turn it on. It only takes a few steps.

Set up 2FA  
( https://clicks.firstrade.com/f/a/b8i85kseJ0FhwqNv2bGvSA~~/AAQRxRA~/iS3yCsuDOSQhDP4rfRKkWDu1romUsbL7O3NjPu8rknkZoqFHEKmKyluRRJcdfEQKFUJUgllEy4NBVhC-GizXE6lt4KSRH10zIECxeBnaXYvkup-nIo92q4EV6uCxZDjUnHdNUHt7_mVj4gmfKBTa3kK62WIOWWQUwIb5-b3uQewuKLNo65j7rtCsaIvCkNlg )


Review your devices with Device Monitoring.
-------------------------------------------

Use Device Monitoring 
( https://clicks.firstrade.com/f/a/bfVQretG28W-TPwYT9_Www~~/AAQRxRA~/0NPd0t22PFdwNev6FPWXMBlgDIm8KmCcCIXLcC-GNRdVWkDERQwO9vmQldSa6_DVL2oceoqE1GhyP29pi0HoeVhjiQsFT4T84HxDaeId4qLRf6zA1eyOIZHuL4V0HDVSnoy9ka7U5vOnBMOphe2xJnrD6qZG4zBKGEqgIzaAEy4Sj0HQInLc9hGOVVpzUVu_WjMVTlb2v620L-9UKv6-Og~~ )
 to review the browsers and devices that access your account and
remove any you don't recognize. We'll email you whenever a new
device successfully logs in.

Use a strong, unique password.
------------------------------

Don't reuse passwords from other websites or apps.

Never share your password or verification codes.
------------------------------------------------

Firstrade will never ask for your password or verification
codes, ask to remotely access your device, or ask you to download
software. If anyone does, it is a scam, even if they claim to be
from Firstrade.

Go directly to official channels.
---------------------------------

Sign in through a bookmark you saved from our official website,
or through the Firstrade app, and contact us only through our
official contact page ( https://clicks.firstrade.com/f/a/VCl3cRqTG4vAyZheT_gKSQ~~/AAQRxRA~/e0RJwVfCBkASsj7vozFalRgADJ7xi_vmg-Tdk5x0kl0fyC_Qqzs7Ggu_Ye3io6WVDOvPbrWSDgjTouti8REJ6EaiBJmljEXgHq9ohwKQbnw797OHkJ5LUZx82NqBrzc-AclhLq1Qd3V9ivBBoRrejQ~~ ) . Please do not rely on phone numbers found through online
searches. Firstrade does not operate client groups on LINE,
WhatsApp, WeChat, Telegram, or similar messaging apps. Please be
cautious of any invitation to join one in our name.

To learn more about how to protect your account, visit our
Security Cente

text:
Three September launches now hold the top three places on the Intelligence Index, plus batch discounts, US and EU in-region routing, and a hosted shell any model can use.

OpenRouter ( https://openrouter.ai?utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio )

September 2026

***************************************
What shipped on OpenRouter in September
***************************************

Claude Opus 5.5 ( https://openrouter.ai/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=hero-opus-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ), Claude Fable 5.1 ( https://openrouter.ai/anthropic/claude-fable-5.1?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=hero-fable-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ), and GPT-6 Astra ( https://openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-6-astra?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=hero-astra-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ) all launched in September, and they now hold the top three places on the Intelligence Index, on the benchmarks board ( https://openrouter.ai/rankings?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=hero-rankings-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ). GPT-6 Sol ( https://openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-6-sol?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=hero-sol-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ), Grok 4.7
( https://openrouter.ai/x-ai/grok-4.7?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=hero-grok-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ), Gemini 3.8 Flash ( https://openrouter.ai/google/gemini-3.8-flash?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=hero-gemini-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ), and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ( https://openrouter.ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=hero-deepseek-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ) landed in the same month, and Jev Router ( https://openrouter.ai/typesafe/jev-router?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=hero-jev-router-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ) can now pick among them for each request.

OpenRouter also released the self-serve Business plan ( https://openrouter.ai/business?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=intro-business-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ) with US and EU in-region routing. The Batch API is live with per-model discounts, typically 50% off the per-token price, and any tool-calling model can now use a hosted shell.

Turn on in-region routing ( https://openrouter.ai/business?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=hero-cta-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio )

In-region routing

--------------------------------
Choose where your inference runs
--------------------------------

Data residency, previously the line between a self-serve account and a sales conversation, is now a base URL. Point a request at us.openrouter.ai or eu.openrouter.ai and OpenRouter decrypts, routes, and serves it inside that region, on the same API key and the same model IDs. If no in-region provider can serve the model, the request returns a 404 instead of quietly leaving the region, and openrouter/auto and other router models are not available on regional domains.

curl https://us.openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENROUTER_API_KEY" \
  -d '{ "model": "anthropic/claude-fable-5.1", ... }'

One line changes: point a service at the regional base URL and leave the rest of your traffic on openrouter.ai. To enforce it, set a guardrail ( https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/guardrails?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=guardrails-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio )'s allowed data regions for a key, a member, or a whole workspace, and OpenRouter rejects that key's, member's, or workspace's requests when they arrive through any other domain. The models page filters to EU-eligible ( https://openrouter.ai/models?data_regions=eu&utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=eu-models-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ) and US-eligible ( https://openrouter.ai/models?data_regions=us&utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=us-models-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ) models.

It ships with the Business plan ( https://openrouter.ai/business?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=business-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ), which any account or organization switches on from its settings, and with Enterprise. The fee is 8% on credit purchases, against 5.5% on Standard; both plans bill inference at provider rates, with no monthly minimum or contract. Business also raises the workspace cap to 1,000. How in-region routing works ( https://openrouter.ai/blog/announcements/us-in-region-routing/?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=irr-blog-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ).

8%

New router

------------------------------------------------------
Jev Router picks the model and effort for each request
------------------------------------------------------

Jev Router runs on Jev ( https://openrouter.ai/~typesafe/jev-latest?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=router-jev-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ), TypeSafe's decision model. Before each turn, Jev scores the prompt on difficulty and precision, and checks whether a bigger model or more effort would help, whether a cheaper model is enough, and whether the task changed.

It keeps a model that works for the rest of the session and raises or lowers effort without switching, so the conversation stays in the cache. It switches only when the expected gain is larger than the cost, including the cache it would lose. Each response includes routing metadata with the reason for the choice, and the routing insights panel in OpenRouter Chat ( https://openrouter.ai/chat?models=typesafe/jev-router&utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=router-chat-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ) shows the model and the scores behind every turn.

Jev reads only the conversation text, never attachments, under zero data retention terms, and requests with zdr: true work with Jev Router. If the Jev call times out or returns invalid output, the request fails instead of falling back to another router. Read about Jev Router ( https://openrouter.ai/typesafe/jev-router?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=router-page-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ).

2

The model behind it

--------------------------------------------------------------
Jev answers typed questions, and your code acts on the answers
--------------------------------------------------------------

typesafe/jev-1.13 is live on OpenRouter through the System One API ( https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/systemone/submit-a-system-one-request?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=jev-systemone-docs-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ). It is a decision model from TypeSafe, and it does not generate text. You send a state (a message, a document, a pending tool call) and typed questions, and it returns typed answers your code can branch on, with a median round trip of 0.24 seconds on OpenRouter.

Try Jev in the playground ( https://openrouter.ai/typesafe/jev-1.13?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=jev-cta-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio#playground )

Jev answers three question types: noul (yes or no), choice (pick one option), and score (a number in a range). Choice and score answers can also carry per-option probabilities and a confidence value, for code that wants to set its own threshold.

Jev reads instructions literally. Keep arithmetic and date comparisons in your code, and send only the state a question needs.

Teams already on the TypeSafe SDK switch by pointing their base URL at openrouter.ai/api and using an OpenRouter key. See the TypeSafe SDK guide ( https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/community/typesafe-sdk?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=jev-sdk-guide-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ).

Two cookbooks show where Jev fits in a pipeline: Gate agent tool calls with Jev ( https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/building-agents/gate-tool-calls-with-jev?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=jev-cookbook-gate-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ) and cut LLM cost with a Jev-verified cascade ( https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/evaluate-and-optimize/jev-verified-cascade?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=jev-cookbook-cascade-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ).

>From launch week

Models that lost ground after Jev's launch

In OpenRouter's launch-week data, the flash versions from many labs lost the most ground. Nearly half of Jev's first users on the platform had not touched any model the week before, so the launch also brought new builders in. See the post ( https://www.linkedin.com/posts/openrouter_q-which-models-have-been-most-impacted-by-activity-7508133133398044673-4mcM?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=linkedin-jev-impact-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ).

Model discounts

Gemini 3.8 Flash is 50% off, Mercury 2.5 is 80% off, GPT-5.6 Sol is 50% off, and Batch requests are 50% off standard per-token pricing.

Current pricing sits on the Gemini 3.8 Flash ( https://openrouter.ai/google/gemini-3.8-flash?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=promo-gemini-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ) and Sol ( https://openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-5.6-sol?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=promo-sol-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ) model pages, alongside every other discounted model ( https://openrouter.ai/collections/discounted-models?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=promo-collection-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ). The Batch API ( https://openrouter.ai/docs/batch-quickstart?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=batch-discount-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ) bills separately, at that same 50% rate on supported models.

Batch API

-------------------------------
Batch discounts, 24-hour window
-------------------------------

The Batch API ( https://openrouter.ai/docs/batch-quickstart?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=batch-docs-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ) is live. Each batch uses one model and one endpoint shape: submit an inline array of requests and collect the results within 24 hours. It accepts chat completions, Responses, Anthropic Messages, and embeddings. Batch requests are typically billed at 50% of the model's per-token price; xAI models are 20% off in batch (Grok 4.3 at $1.00 / $2.00 against $1.25 / $2.50), and web search and prompt caching bill at their usual rates. Models with batch support list a :batch variant with the batch rate, for example openai/gpt-6-astra:batch at $5/M input. Batches are text-only.

POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/batches
{ "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "model": "openai/gpt-6-astra",
  "requests": [ { "custom_id": "req-0001", "body": { ... } } ] }

The batch rankings ( https://openrouter.ai/rankings/batch?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=batch-rankings-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ) page shows weekly usage of batch models across OpenRouter.

Read the Batch API quickstart ( https://openrouter.ai/docs/batch-quickstart?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=batch-cta-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio )

Server tools

-----------------------------------------
A hosted shell for any tool-calling model
-----------------------------------------

Add openrouter:shell to the tools array and any tool-calling model can run commands in a hosted Linux container. The model writes a script, runs it, reads stderr, fixes it, and then answers. openrouter:bash does the same for the Anthropic tool shape, and the Files API stores up to 10 GiB per workspace for containers to read and write.

Sandbox time costs $0.0001 per active second, billed inside the request. Both tools are in beta, and workspace admins can switch any server tool off. Read the announcement ( https://openrouter.ai/blog/announcements/shell-tool/?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=shell-blog-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ).

Server tools docs ( https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/server-tools?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=server-tools-docs-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio )

From the image gallery, select several models and open them in Chat with the benchmark prompt carried over. Insights

-------------------------
What the usage data shows
-------------------------

As of September 8, GPT-5.6 Luna was the only closed model in the top 10 by token volume over the prior 30 days, and number two overall. By the data page's classification, February 6 may have been the last day when humans consumed more tokens through OpenRouter than agents did. And as of late August, the three things people most paid AI to do were executing workflows through agents, generating code, and classifying things at volume. The charts and the sources behind each of these sit on the data page ( https://openrouter.ai/data?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=data-page-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio ), alongside the rankings and the research that cites them.

OpenRouter also publishes Inferred, a weekly newsletter built from this same data. Its first issue covers how OpenAI and Anthropic split spend and how far the open-weight labs have closed the gap.

Explore the data ( https://openrouter.ai/data?utm_campaign=092826-sept-recap-wide&utm_content=data-cta-b&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customerio )
